item.title: [ 34] I'm thinking about the Kids Act and the long-term crackdown of the internet. Bu
item.description:
I'm thinking about the Kids Act and the long-term crackdown of the internet. But actually, this perspective is wrong. Because the internet is already dead. And it wasn't killed by laws, but by AI. It's dead because we can no longer know who is human and who isn't. And it's precisely on imageboards that it's particularly difficult, if not impossible, to identify bots. That's why it would be absolutely no loss if all the small social platforms/forums were to disappear completely tomorrow. They're already dead. I've become aware here of that, because there is an extremely large number of "anons" who are sucking up to the super-rich, the Big Tech corporations and sloptubers. At first, I was surprised that there are so many system cucks on /g/. No. They're bots. Bots that were deployed to control the narrative. We have absolutely nothing left to lose because we've already lost everything. I believe that 4chan is by far the most artificial platform of all. And the insidious thing about the whole thing is that it simultaneously offers the best simulation of "authenticity." We're definitely no better than the Facebook boomers who fall for AI crap. Our AI crap is simply text-based.

item.title: [ 30] Vance tells Americans not to ‘gripe about all the little things’ as cost of living soars
item.description:
Vance tells Sean Hannity that Democratic ‘arsonists’ will reverse Trump’s successes even as he admits his own administration needs more time

https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/jd-vance-voters-midterms-gasoline-b3060535.html

Vice President JD Vance laid out the Trump administration’s best case for a Republican victory in the midterm elections on Thursday, returning to his role as the White House’s great communicator. But instead of empathizing with Americans’ economic pains and fears about the future, the vice president leaned into fear-mongering about Democrats.

Vance spoke with Fox’s Sean Hannity in an interview that aired Thursday, and leaned into the administration’s successes at driving illegal crossings at the U.S.-Mexico border to 50-year lows as he made the case for the GOP.

As he spoke about the supposed priorities of hypothetical Democratic majorities in the House and Senate, however, Vance claimed that his opponents wanted to block Republicans from ever winning elections again and “transform” America, citing such issues as acceptance of transgender Americans.

He claimed those reasons were why Americans should not “gripe” about the “little things” like gas prices nearing their Covid-era highs, U.S. casualties in the war against Iran and high cost of living issues, and give Republicans two more years to attempt to fix things.

“This is not the time to sort of gripe about all the little things. There are obviously — I think every single person who voted for us in 2024 could find something where they wish maybe congressional Republicans had gone further,” said Vance.

“But the challenge here is between Democrats who want to destroy the country, who want to permanently disempower you, make it so even if you vote Republican your vote doesn’t actually count anymore. And Republicans, who fundamentally are trying to solve the problems that Democrats under Joe Biden created. That is the choice.”

item.title: [ 39] Trump’s powerful new friends are making MAGA uncomfortable
item.description:
https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6124669-trump-xi-mamdani-gop-concerns/

President Trump’s appearances with Chinese President Xi Jinping, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) and leaders from Silicon Valley risk turning off his political base just as Republicans are seeking to turbocharge turnout ahead of the midterms, say GOP strategists.

The president has always loved meeting with the powerful, even if they are dictators or democratic socialists, as it makes headlines and highlights his own stature.

Trump was the first president to meet with North Korea leader Kim Jong Un, and he met with Russian President Vladimir Putin last year. He had a memorable buddy-buddy term in the Oval Office with Mamdani last November, even as his party sought to vilify the liberal mayor.

To many Republicans, the latest meetings are a danger.

“Frankly, it’s inexplicable,” one unnamed Republican strategist said. “Not because as president you shouldn’t meet with the Chinese president or event the mayor of New York, but given their toxicity with the base that you were desperate to try to turnout at higher than normal levels to try and offset your vulnerabilities with every other layer of the November turnout populace.”

“You need to fire up your base and instead you’re kind of deflating them in the homestretch,” the strategist added.

Trump hosted his Chinese counterpart last week for a lavish state visit at the White House. That meeting came after Mamdani hosted Trump at Gracie Mansion in New York City.

On Tuesday, Trump invited several tech leaders to the White House for a luncheon on artificial intelligence before appearing with them on the White House North Lawn for an impromptu news conference.

Polling shows that the president’s base views China with skepticism.

item.description:
https://www.foxnews.com/politics/aocs-dramatic-retelling-cornell-rape-allegations-collides-complaint-details
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., painted a far more sweeping picture of a Cornell University sexual assault case than what's alleged in the underlying civil complaint, while also making claims the university disputes.

Speaking during a town hall hosted by More Perfect University on Sunday in Ithaca, New York, Ocasio-Cortez addressed allegations outlined in a civil complaint filed last month by a former Cornell student identified as Jane Doe, who alleges she was drugged and sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members in October 2024.

"Seven men drugged and gang raped a 20-year-old woman," Ocasio-Cortez said.

"They lured her in to a fraternity house," she continued. "They drugged her with ketamine. They then posted to a group chat that she was incapacitated, and seven men took turns gang raping her for seven hours."
"Their fraternity knew. This was reported to Cornell University. And after looking into this matter, they expelled two of them and made the rest write essays as their form of punishment," Ocasio-Cortez said. "I want to be clear that the culture of rape, sexual assault, and pedophilia is protected in elite institutions across the United States and including Cornell University in this instance. It has got to stop."

Cornell has disputed Ocasio-Cortez's characterization of the disciplinary action, saying expulsions and suspensions were issued and that no respondent was required to write an essay as the sole consequence. The civil complaint alleges that several students who received temporary suspensions were given an opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to the university.

item.title: [173] Real Traveler's map™ thread
item.description:
Post your travel maps in this thread. Pic related is the official /trv/ Real Traveler's map™, edition 4.0.5. I am remaking this general after almost a year of it being dead, so this is not the usual OP.

Fill in the countries and subdivisions you have visited, talk about your map and ask others about their maps. You can use the map however you like, the colors are more like suggestions, you don't have to use them, and you don't have to use all of them. You can add or remove colors and change the map as much as you want in any way you want. Don't like this map? Upload a completely different one. Up to you. Despite what some might say, there's no "wrong" way to use the map, and new posters and less travelled people are welcome and encouraged to stay and post :) This map is a group effort by our board, and we can only improve it if people reach out to share suggestions or corrections.

This is the newest edition of the map, edition 4.0.5, updated for September 2025. Thanks to an Anon in previous threads, it is now easier than ever to fill in the map. You can use the website splored.com to easily color in entire countries with a single click. At the time of making this thread, it uses the old 4.0.4 template, so you still need to update it to 4.0.5 with the simplified template, but hopefully it will be updated.

item.title: [143] NYC 7 DAY ITINERARY
item.description:
>Mon — Times Square. Top of the Rock. Dinner at Bubba Gump.

>Tue — Statue of Liberty ferry. Little Italy lunch. Dinner at Carmine's.

>Wed — Empire State Building. Macy's Herald Square. Dinner at Tao. 169 Bar.

>Thu — 9/11 Memorial. Charging Bull photo. Lexington Candy Shop (This 97 year old diner still serves their Coke the old-fashioned way). Dinner at Eataly.

>Fri — SoHo shopping. Magnolia Bakery. Katz's dinner. Times Square The Basement rave

>Sat — Brooklyn Bridge walk at noon. DUMBO photos. 9/11 memorial. Dinner at Lombardi's. Times Square.

>Sun — Central Park horse carriage. Brunch at Sarabeth's. Broadway matinee. Charging bull photo.

>Mon – Check-out. Final pilgrimage with my luggage to Lexington & 125th cause of the velvet underground song. Blacklane ride to JFK.

My idea is to have a good time and make it an unforgettable experience at the city that never sleeps. Something that will change me forever.
